terms.gloss: turn down the heat, draw off some of the fire
terms.grammar: subtrahō, subtrahere, subtrāxī, subtractum, with ignem
evidence: Col. 12.20.4: cum deinde ad tertiās subsēderit coctūra, subtrahe ignem
Apic. 1.1.1: subtractō ignī in sē redit
terms.comment: On a hearth the heat is the fire itself, and the cook turns it down by drawing some of it out from under the pot. The words serve for a stove today. For turning it up we have found no instance in a kitchen; ignem augēre is ours (see the examples).

terms.grammar: ablative; also lēnī ignī, ad ignem lēnem
evidence: Col. 12.42.2: lentō ignī, nē adūrantur, carbōnibus dēcoquuntur
terms.comment: The usual words for a gentle fire: Columella’s lentō ignī, Cato’s lēnī ignī, Apicius’s ad ignem lēnem and lentō ignī. For a high heat we have found no set phrase; Vitruvius speaks of a pot on a fire vehementī fervōre (8.3.3), and ācrī ignī would be ours.

terms.gloss: take off the heat, take the fire away
terms.grammar: subdūcō, subdūcere, subdūxī, subductum, with ignem
evidence: Cato Agr. 105: ignem subditō. Ubi bullābit vīnum, ignem subdūcitō
terms.comment: Cato’s pair: ignem subdere, put the fire under (put it on the heat), and ignem subdūcere, take it away. Columella says ab igne removēre of taking the pot off the fire; see the examples.

phrases.latin: Jūs fervet; subtrahe ignem, ut lentō ignī coquātur.
phrases.english: The soup is boiling; turn the heat down so it cooks slowly.
The water isn’t boiling yet; turn up the heat.

phrases.latin: Posteā ignī lēnī coquitō, rudiculā agitātō crēbrō
phrases.english: Then cook it on a low heat, stirring often with a wooden spoon

phrases.latin: quae cum īnferbuerit, tāleolās inulae adjicitō et statim ab igne removētō
phrases.english: when it has come to the boil, add the slips of elecampane and take it off the heat at once

phrases.latin: Musti Q. XX in ahēneum aut plumbeum īnfunditō, ignem subditō. Ubi bullābit vīnum, ignem subdūcitō.
phrases.english: Pour twenty quadrantals of must into a bronze or lead pot and light the fire under it. When the wine bubbles, take the fire away.
